one_liner: Open-source (MIT) Python CLI that searches for a username across hundreds of social networks; there is no hosted service or API.
notes: Sherlock is a local CLI (pipx/pip/uv/docker/dnf) with no accounts, keys or hosted endpoint, so auth_methods=other (local tool with no auth, as the rubric says) and access=self_serve_free (MIT, free to install; there are no credentials to gate). api_style=sdk_or_cli_only: the README only documents the CLI. The org does have a repo 'sherlock-project/api', which is a self-hosted Django REST Framework wrapper that you run yourself on 127.0.0.1:8000. It is not a hosted public API, so I did not count it as rest. MCP: I checked the sherlock-project org repos (sherlock, sherlockproject.xyz, .github, build, api) and the README: there is no official MCP server. A web search for 'sherlock username search MCP server' found third-party ones: Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp (GitHub, PyPI sherlock-mcp, glama), OSINT bundles (frishtik/osint-tools-mcp-server, OpenOSINT) and Apify actors exposed over Apify's MCP. So mcp=community. Verdict=blocked with main_blocker=not_a_saas because there is no public hosted API, as the task's edge-case guidance says. An agent could still shell out to the CLI or run a community MCP server locally, so this verdict is the field most open to argument.
